Use N–mm–MPa units throughout.
Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic solid mechanics.
Assume the shaft is solid and circular with uniform cross-section.
Assume the angle-of-twist limit is the governing design criterion.
Assume transverse shear loading does not contribute to the angle of twist.
Let L = 1500 mm.
Let G = 25939.8 MPa.
Let T = 1,000,000 N·mm.
Let phi_allow = 0.75 degrees, converted to 0.01308997 radians.
Use the governing relation phi = T L / (J G).
Use J = pi d^4 / 32 for a solid circular shaft.
Solve for the minimum diameter from d = (32 T L / (pi G phi_allow))^(1/4).
Substitute the given values to obtain d approximately 81.9 mm.
Round up to the nearest practical size to satisfy the limit.
Specify the minimum required diameter as 82 mm.
